blocks.content: The Governor is the head of the State while the Chief Minister is the head of the government.

rows: Appointed by the President of India
Acts on the aid and advice of the Council
Heads and leads the Council of Ministers

items: Questions frequently distinguish between the nominal powers of the Governor and the real executive powers exercised by the Chief Minister.
Direct questions often ask about Article 167 (duties of Chief Minister regarding communication of administrative decisions to the Governor).
Exam questions regularly test the rule allowing a non-legislator to remain Chief Minister for up to six months.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Governor is the nominal executive authority (de jure executive), whereas the Chief Minister is the real executive authority (de facto executive).
Article 164 specifies that the Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor, who traditionally invites the leader of the majority party in the state legislative assembly.
A person who is not a member of the state legislature can be appointed as Chief Minister, but must get elected to either house within six months.
The Chief Minister holds office during the pleasure of the Governor, but cannot be dismissed as long as they retain majority support in the assembly.
Article 167 acts as a bridge between the Governor and the Council of Ministers, defining the constitutional duties of the Chief Minister to furnish information.
